text:
aj: noticing a spike of ALB target deregisters in eu-west-2 around 12:03 UTC, looks correlated with a NAT IP refresh on the egress fleet
emma: saw that, noticed readiness probes timing out rather than 5xx responses :thinking_face:
samir: can you paste the ALB logs? curious if it's 504/timeout or connection refused
aj: pasting snippet from alb access logs: 
```
eu-west-2-alb 10.0.4.12:443 10.0.5.18:31415 0.000 0.012 0.100 504 "GET /healthz HTTP/1.1" 503 0 0 0 "ELB-HealthChecker/2.0" - -
```

lia: interesting, ALB shows 504 but pod logs show no request arriving around those timestamps
aj: my theory: SNAT IP rotation -> ephemeral port churn -> conntrack/GW NAT translation not populated -> ALB healthcheck hits node but SNAT mapping missing so packets dropped before reaching kube-proxy
emma: we also saw a brief increase in conntrack table size before the events, I have metrics: `conntrack_count` jumped from ~32k to 47k in 30s
samir: if conntrack GC can't reclaim quickly, new outbound flows for healthchecks could fail until mapping established. That would look like probe timeouts and ALB deregistering after 10s of failed checks
lia: ops-bot reported a NAT gateway replacement at 12:02:58 UTC (scheduled), that coincides with the timing
ops-bot: NAT-gateway-rotations: started replacement nat-gtw-23 -> completed nat-gtw-47 (12:02:58 - 12:03:25 UTC)
aj: confirming timeline: NAT swap -> short conntrack spike -> ALB healthchecks time out -> targets marked unhealthy -> deregisters -> traffic fails over to other zone
emma: mitigation options: extend ALB unhealthy threshold, increase conntrack table and reduce GC delay, or avoid simultaneous NAT rotations in multiple AZs
samir: immediate patch: bump conntrack max to 200k on edge nodes and tune nf_conntrack_generic_timeout to prune more aggressively. Also can add iptables rule to accept ALB healthcheck source CIDRs to bypass SNAT?
lia: note: bypassing SNAT for healthchecks might require nodePort exposure and affects security posture, needs review with security team
aj: I deployed a canary sysctl change to one node pool (testing) `net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=200000` and `nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_established=600`. we'll monitor
deploy-bot: canary change deployed to pool edge-canary-1 at 12:10 UTC (k8s DaemonSet sysctl-override:v2)
emma: watching dashboards, conntrack_count on canary nodes dropped GC pressure, ALB re-registered targets for canary instances within 30s
samir: long term: propose we implement staggered NAT rotations across AZs + prewarm conntrack entries for healthcheck flows before swapping gateway IPs
lia: also adding a short-term runbook: if ALB mass-deregistrations detected, check NAT rotation window, bump conntrack if needed, temporarily increase ALB healthy thresholds and coord with netops
aj: will open an incident runbook PR and schedule a retro with netops. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
emma: adding action items to infra board: [1] runbook PR, [2] conntrack autosizing proposal, [3] NAT rotation policy change
samir: adding a note: verify if any on-prem private deployment customers saw similar probe flaps during our NAT maintenance windows
lia: tagging @oncall for visibility and security review ticket creation
aj: closing the temporary alert for eu-west-2 once rollouts complete
deploy-bot: alert eu-west-2-alb-targets was silenced by aj for 30m at 12:25 UTC
